title: Yellow leaf curl virus in outdoor tomatoes

Header: Yellow leaf curl virus in outdoor tomatoes
Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV) Virusi njano kujikunja majani, rasta, bondia in Swahili

Prevention: Tengeru 97); no resistant variety is available.

Monitoring: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus disease can infect all growth stages but is most problematic in young stages.
Search for small leaves rolled upward from the edges forming a cup-shape.
Leaves become yellow between veins and at leaf edges.
This virus is not transmitted by soil or in the air, and not by seeds.
It is transmitted mainly by whiteflies.
When plants with virus symptoms are observed in the field, consider action.
Slightly shake plants in seed beds or young plantings to check for white flies.
When white flies fly off from 5 - 10 plants, they need to be controlled.
If there are no virus symptoms, some whiteflies can be tolerated.
Infected pepper plants will show no symptoms of virus infection but whiteflies can pick up and spread the virus.
Direct Control: Regularly uproot all diseased plants; bury, or put in plastic bags in the field and burn outside field.
Viruses cannot be controlled, but the insects that spread the virus can.
